title: XXII: The Procession

teacherSummary.text: The procession passes; Dimmesdale walks with strange energy and seems far from Hester. Mistress Hibbins tells Hester she knows the minister's secret. Hester stands by the scaffold listening to the sermon's tone through the meetinghouse walls. Pearl brings the captain's message: Chillingworth will bring the minister aboard.

segments.script: First, meaning. I read “We must not always talk in the marketplace of what happens to us in the forest” slowly and put it in my own words: Hester tells Pearl they must not talk in the marketplace about what happens in the forest. Next, craft. I notice the two places stand for two worlds: the town's public law and the private freedom of the woods. The strongest word is “forest”: it stands for the hidden, natural life where she and Dimmesdale were honest with each other. Then, effect. What does Hester mean by keeping the forest out of the marketplace? My answer: By keeping the forest out of the marketplace, Hester means their private plans from the forest must stay hidden in town; the line shows how secrecy divides private truth from public life.
